answer: Response-order delay curve.** Each identity's first message is held until it lands in a distinct slot of the network's arrival tide, and slots are assigned by hashing the identity against the prior epoch's traffic histogram. A mirror check re-runs the histogram with the new arrival folded in; if the shape shifts beyond a set threshold, the slot is invalidated. A prism check splits the epoch into sub-windows and requires the identity to appear in more than one, so burst-registered clones cannot share a slot.
